evals.name: from-scratch-with-data
evals.prompt: I need a short deck for Thursday's leadership sync, as a bento slides file (bento.page). Topic: the migration of our ingest pipeline from the old batch jobs to the streaming service. Feel: technical, calm, editorial. Palette: deep green almost black background (#0E1A14), off-white text (#EDE9DF), one accent in warm yellow (#F2B233). Type: a serif display face with a utilitarian sans for body, your pick. Content: (1) a cover; (2) why we did it: nightly batch took 6h and failed roughly one night in five, streaming gives us sub-minute freshness; (3) the numbers: p95 freshness went 6h → 40s, failed runs/month went 6 → 0, infra cost went $18.4k → $11.2k/month, on-call pages went 14 → 3 per month; (4) a before/after comparison of batch vs streaming on: freshness, failure handling, cost, replay ability, ops burden; (5) what's left: backfill tooling, the two legacy consumers still on batch, retiring the old cluster by end of Q4; (6) a closing ask: approve retiring the batch cluster. Put speaker notes on each slide, I'll talk from them. Save it as Ingest_Migration.bento.html in the output folder.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained Ingest_Migration.bento.html with a valid bento/slides document: cover, a chart for the before/after numbers (not text), a table for the comparison, morph or stable-id chrome, speaker notes on every slide, the given palette, embedded or system fonts, no text overflow. Plus evidence the author rendered and inspected the slides.
assertions: Ingest_Migration.bento.html exists and its #bento-doc block parses as a bento/slides doc with 6+ slides
The before/after numbers get a numeric treatment (a chart with plain-number series, or stat elements with count-up), not body text
The batch-vs-streaming comparison is a table element
At least one slide uses transition morph and shares an element id with the previous slide
Every slide has non-empty speaker notes
Palette honoured: theme.background #0E1A14 and theme.accent #F2B233
At most two font families across text elements (a third only if monospace)
Every non-system font family is embedded in doc.fonts
No thin accent rule sitting directly under a title (generated-slide hallmark)
Runtime validate() reports no errors and no text-overflow warnings
Per-slide screenshots exist in the outputs (evidence the deck was rendered and inspected)

evals.name: edit-existing-deck
evals.prompt: Here's my deck 'Platform Review.bento.html' (it's a bento slides file). Add two slides before the closing number slide: one with a bar chart of monthly active workspaces for Jan–Jun (1,240 / 1,310 / 1,480 / 1,620 / 1,910 / 2,260) and one three-column slide titled 'What drove it' with columns: 'SSO launch' (enterprise trials doubled after the March SSO release), 'Template gallery' (new workspaces created from a template went from 12% to 41%), 'Faster imports' (median import time fell from 9 min to 40 s). Match the existing look exactly, keep the speaker notes style, don't touch the other slides. Save the result over the same file in the output folder.
evals.expected_output: The same file with 5 slides: the original 3 in place and unchanged, a chart slide with plain-number bar data, a three-column slide built from the deck's existing presets (same fonts, colors, eyebrow/title positions). docId unchanged, notes on the new slides, validate clean, and no overflow.
assertions: The file still parses as a bento/slides document
docId unchanged
Exactly 5 slides, with the two new ones inserted before the closing number slide
The original three slides are unchanged (deep-equal to the input)
A bar chart element carries the six monthly values as plain numbers
New slides reuse the deck's existing font stacks and colours
The three-column slide follows the existing eyebrow (y 72) + title (y 104) layout at x 96
Three column heads sit at the band's 3-column x positions (96, 470, 844)
The two new slides have speaker notes
Runtime validate() reports no errors and no text-overflow warnings
Screenshots of the result exist in the outputs (evidence it was rendered and inspected)
